name: Granite Creek Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground along Wild & Scenic Granite Creek near Granite Hot Springs, ~10 mi up Granite Creek Rd (gravel FR 30500) off US-189/191 SE of Jackson. 53 sites, potable water, vault toilets, no hookups; RVs up to ~45 ft. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. Granite Hot Springs pool ~0.7 mi N. --Claude

name: Green River Lakes Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground near Lower Green River Lake at the N end of the Wind River Range, ~50 mi N of Pinedale via Green River Lakes Rd (FR 650). 36 single sites first-come, first-served (plus 3 reservable group sites), vault toilets. Long rough gravel road (2WD-passable when dry, impassable when wet); water was unavailable in 2026 due to Dollar Lake Fire damage - better for smaller/mid rigs; verify conditions before going. --Claude

name: Half Moon Lake Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground off the NE shore of Half Moon Lake, ~9 mi NE of Pinedale at ~7,600 ft. 17 sites (3 with direct lake access), vault toilets, no drinking water; sites screened by willows. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. Narrow, partly unpaved access with limited turnaround - tight for large rigs, best for smaller/mid RVs. --Claude

name: Hams Fork Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground on the Big Spring Scenic Backway (Hams Fork Rd, FR 10062) ~38 mi N of Kemmerer. 13 sites on either side of the access road (western sites near the Hams Fork River), potable water, vault toilets, summer trash service; tent & RV camping, first-come, first-served. No cell service. --Claude

name: Hog Park Campground
note: Medicine Bow-Routt NF, 50 sites in three loops on the SE shore of Hog Park Reservoir at ~8,400 ft, with boat ramp. 27 reservable sites (loops 1-2, to ~30 ft); the 22-site back loop is FCFS and recommended for tents/small campers (tight turning radius). Vault toilets, drinking water. Access is ~18 mi of washboard gravel. --Claude

name: Hunter Peak Campground
note: Shoshone NF (Clarks Fork RD), 10-site campground on the banks of the Clarks Fork of the Yellowstone River at ~6,500 ft on the Chief Joseph Scenic Hwy (WY-296). Currently first-come, first-served; vault toilets, hand-pump water, bear boxes, food-storage required. Max spur ~32 ft. --Claude

name: Island Park Campground
note: Bighorn NF, 9 single-family sites on West Tensleep Creek ~21 mi NE of Ten Sleep off US-16, near the Cloud Peak Wilderness. Mostly reservable (one FCFS site); vault toilets, hand-pump water, no hookups; nearest dump ~17 mi. --Claude

name: Jack Creek Campground
note: Shoshone NF (Greybull RD, W of Meeteetse via WY-290/FR), 16 first-come, first-served sites along Jack Creek near the Wood River. Single vault toilet, no bear boxes (secure own food); washboard access road. Posted access limit ~22 ft (a 23-ft rig is borderline). Different campground from the Medicine Bow-Routt Jack Creek. --Claude

name: Libby Creek Willow Campground
note: Medicine Bow-Routt NF, 16 sites in the Libby Creek Recreation Area off the Snowy Range Scenic Byway (Hwy 130 / FR-351) at ~8,600 ft, on Libby Creek. Mix of reservable and FCFS sites; vault toilets, seasonal hand-pump water, no hookups. Trailers under ~22 ft (a 23-ft rig is borderline). --Claude

name: Lily Lake Campground
note: Shoshone NF (Clarks Fork RD), small drive-in camping area on Lily Lake off the Beartooth Hwy (US-212) via FR-128, with a boat launch. Reconstructed to ~7 sites; donations, first-come, first-served, no potable water; shared bear boxes. Mix of tent and RV sites, primitive/rustic. --Claude

name: Moran Vista Camping Area
note: Bridger-Teton NF designated dispersed area off FR30290 (Spread Creek Rd), ~2.5 mi gravel passable for most RVs. Large level gravel area for self-contained rigs with Teton views; no hookups/facilities (porta-potties only). $10, first-come, first-served, 5-day limit. --Claude

name: North Fork Campground
note: Medicine Bow NF (Snowy Range), off FR101/Sand Lake Rd ~4 mi W of Centennial at ~9,200 ft on the North Fork of the Little Laramie River. 60 sites in two sections, no hookups; some sites along the river. Mix of reservable and FCFS via recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Pole Mountain Dispersed Camping Area
note: Medicine Bow NF, Pole Mountain/Vedauwoo unit - ~97 designated dispersed sites on hard-gravel FR700 (2WD, wide enough for RVs to pass) off Vedauwoo Glen Rd. Rock fire rings only, no water/toilets/trash; most sites fit large RVs (some spurs rutted). First-come, first-served, 16-day limit; road closed Feb-May. --Claude

name: Reuter Campground
note: Black Hills NF (Bearlodge RD), ~3 mi N of Sundance on FSR838 in ponderosa pine at the Reuter Trailhead. Standard sites (some fit 40-ft RVs), potable water/vault toilets, no hookups; front loop reservable, back loop FCFS. Reservable via recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Rex Hale Campground
note: Shoshone NF, North Fork Hwy (US-14/16/20) ~36 mi W of Cody on the North Fork Shoshone River. 30 sites, RVs to 40 ft, ~8 sites with electric/water; food-storage lockers, potable water/vault toilets. Reservable and FCFS via recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Wapiti Campground
note: Shoshone NF, Wapiti RD, on the North Fork of the Shoshone River ~30 mi W of Cody on the Buffalo Bill Scenic Byway, ~5,950 ft, by the historic Wapiti Ranger Station. 41 sites — sites 1-21 have 15/30-amp electric, 22-40 nonelectric; RVs to 35+ ft, vault toilets, drinking water, bear boxes. First-come, first-served (online reservations currently suspended). --Claude

name: Pioneer Park
note: City of Torrington municipal park; 18 RV sites with concrete pads, 30/50-amp electric + water (no sewer), dump station; camping at the south end near the North Platte River; first-come, first-served, 10-day limit. Restrooms (no showers). --Claude

name: Albany County Fairgrounds
note: Albany County-owned fairgrounds with a standing campground: 21 full-hookup + 6 electric-only sites, 30/50-amp, open 24/7 year-round; first-come, first-served (self-pay station), 14-day limit. Enter via the north (white-arch) entrance. --Claude

name: Riverside City Park
note: City of Douglas riverfront park on the North Platte River; first-come, first-served overnight RV camping on a U-shaped graveled loop, no hookups but potable water + free dump station, restrooms with showers; 2-night limit, across from the state fairgrounds. --Claude

name: Wheatland City Park (Lewis Park)
note: Town of Wheatland municipal park (Lewis Park); ~15 gravel sites, ~6 with 20/30/50-amp electric, potable water hydrants + dump station; donation, no reservations, 3-night limit; RVs to ~30 ft; UP railroad adjacent (train noise). --Claude

name: Fort Laramie City Park
note: Town of Fort Laramie municipal park; large open drive-in RV spaces, restrooms, three frost-free water hydrants, playground/grills, no hookups; donation (self-pay box), first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Lander City Park
note: City of Lander municipal park on the Middle Fork Popo Agie River; donation, first-come, first-served camping, gravel RV parking + grassy tent areas, seasonal restrooms, no hookups; 3-day max within any 30 days; walkable to downtown. --Claude

name: Sweetwater Events Complex - RV Park
note: Sweetwater County events complex in Rock Springs with 1,200+ full-hookup RV sites (nearly all 50 amp) across three campgrounds (Boar's Tusk, Pilot Butte, White Mountain); open to the public between events, first-come first-served, restroom/shower facilities. --Claude

name: Mikesell-Potts Recreation Area
note: Johnson County recreation area on the south shore of Lake DeSmet, 8 mi N of Buffalo off I-90 exit 51; 60+ first-come first-served campsites (8 with electric), two boat ramps, vault restrooms -- NO potable water or dump station. --Claude

name: Horseshoe Bend Campground (Bighorn Canyon NRA)
note: NPS campground in Bighorn Canyon National Recreation Area, ~14 mi north of Lovell on a high-desert bench above Bighorn Lake. 68 RV/tent sites, 28 with water+electric hookups, 3 pull-throughs, flush toilets, dump station; marina/boat ramp/swim beach under 1 mi away. Mostly first-come, first-served (a few sites reservable online). --Claude

name: Saratoga Lake Campground
note: Town of Saratoga campground on Saratoga Lake, 1 mi north of town: 50 electric (30/50A) sites and 34 non-electric, big-rig capable, sandy swim beach and boat access; water is non-potable. First-come, first-served (open May-Oct, plus the January ice-fishing derby). --Claude

name: Station Creek Campground
note: USFS (Bridger-Teton NF) campground in Snake River Canyon along the Wild & Scenic Snake River, ~27 mi SW of Jackson on US-26/89. 16 single sites are first-come, first-served; only the separate group site is reservable. Vault toilets, no hookups, lodgepole shade; popular for fly-fishing and rafting. --Claude

name: Twin Bridges Area at Grand Lake State Park
note: Twin Bridges Area of Grand Lake State Park at the Neosho/Spring river confluence; 60 RV sites with water/electric plus 100 tent sites, dump station and lighted boat ramps; RV sites reservable online (tent sites first-come, first-served). --Claude

name: Alabaster Caverns State Park
note: Mesa Campground at Alabaster Caverns SP near Freedom. 23 reservable RV sites (pull-thru & back-in) with 30/50-amp electric, plus FCFS primitive tent sites; dump station, hot showers; open year-round even when the cave closes. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica. --Claude

name: Caney Bend (Hulah Lake)
note: USACE Hulah Lake public-use area (Caney River arm), a primitive drive-in RV camping loop (listed RVs-only). No hookups; first-come, first-served, not on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Hackberry Bend Campground - Beaver Dunes Park
note: Hackberry Bend Campground in Beaver Dunes Park, a City of Beaver park 1 mi N of Beaver (Oklahoma State Parks transferred it to the city; the legislature approved it in 2012), a distinct loop ~0.4 mi from Pioneer near the park's two-acre lake and the sand dunes. 7 RV sites with 20/30/50-amp electric and water plus ~10 tent sites and a primitive cabin; dump station, showers. Not on ReserveAmerica; call the park. TravelOK's listing (undated, read 2026-10-20) gives $25 a night. --Claude

name: Buckhorn Campground
note: NPS Chickasaw National Recreation Area campground on the eastern shore of Lake of the Arbuckles. 134 tent/RV sites in four loops with 30/50-amp electric (Loops C/D have some electric+water); Loop C reservable, Loops A/B/D first-come, first-served. No cell service. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Flat Rock Creek
note: USACE Fort Gibson Lake campground on a protected cove near Chouteau; 30 electric family sites plus 1 non-electric FCFS site, flush/pit toilets, showers, drinking water, dump station, boat ramp; seasonal. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Rocky Point
note: USACE Fort Gibson Lake campground on the upper lake where Flat Rock Creek meets the main channel; 59 electric sites + 3 canopy no-hookup FCFS sites, sandy swim beach, playground, flush/pit toilets, showers, 2 dump stations, 3 boat ramps, courtesy dock; year-round. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Skipout
note: USFS campground on Skipout Lake in Black Kettle National Grassland (Cibola NF); 12 units, paved access, drive-in sites (a class-C/26-ft rig reported, ~2 RV-suitable spurs), water spigot + vault toilets, boat ramp, no hookups. First-come, first-served, not on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Winding Stair
note: USFS Ouachita NF campground atop Winding Stair Mtn on the Talimena Scenic Byway; 23 sites with paved spurs (4 doubles, 2 ADA), gravel tent pads, vault toilets, no water/electric; adjacent Emerald Vista overlook and Ouachita Trail trailhead. First-come, first-served (pay on-site or via rec.gov app). --Claude

name: Guy Sandy Campground
note: NPS Chickasaw NRA primitive campground on the western shore of Lake of the Arbuckles; ~40 sites, RVs permitted (limit ~40 ft) but no hookups, water spigots + pit toilets, fire rings, boat access. Open seasonally (about Memorial Day-Labor Day), first-come, first-served, not reservable. --Claude

name: Spring Creek
note: USFS campground on 47-acre Spring Creek Lake in Black Kettle National Grassland (Cibola NF); 5 units along the lakeshore with picnic tables, fire rings, 2 concrete-slab shelters, vault toilets, limited water, dirt boat ramp; accommodates small-to-medium RVs, no hookups. First-come, first-served, not on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Cabin RV Park
note: Ten 80-ft full-hookup pull-thru pads (30/50-amp, W/S) behind Cabin Diesel Services in Big Cabin, ~1 mi from I-44; open year-round, honor-system check-in (no reservations), on-site truck service and propane. Good Sam/FMCA discounts. --Claude

name: Kiowa Park I
note: USACE campground on the shore of Waurika Lake NW of Waurika; 166 drive-in sites, all water + 30/50-amp electric (RVs to ~80 ft), shoreline spur sites, swim beach, boat ramp, showers; two waterfront group sites. Reservable online May-Sept, FCFS Sept 30-Oct 31. --Claude
